title: Finite-cover sections of locally constant pro-etale sets on a normal scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Assume that every local ring of $X$ is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Assume that $F$ is locally constant: there is a pro-etale covering family $\{U_i\to X\}_i$ on each member of which $F$ is isomorphic to the constant sheaf associated to a set $S_i$, meaning the sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Assume also that $F$ is locally nonempty: there is a pro-etale covering family $\{V_j\to X\}_j$ and an element of $F(V_j)$ for every $j$.

Then there exists a finite etale surjective morphism $p:Y\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category, def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that $F(Y)\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9 (Loc_X = Cov_X), pp. 67-68; proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71 (every connected geometric covering is finite etale). Normality supplies geometric unibranchness by Stacks properties.tex Tag 0BQ3, lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch.

proof.text: Restrict the given cover to a u+1-small covering subfamily. Composition of weakly etale maps is left adjoint to base change; uniqueness of left adjoints and sheafification identify the stated inverse image with sectionwise restriction. The cover gives CoversTop at the identity object. Apply [lem-a1-proetale-local-system-representability], obtaining Z in universe u+1, an etale q:Z→X↑ with unique valuation lifting, and the natural functor-of-points isomorphism on the original site.

Choose x in X and a point v of a member V of the local-nonemptiness cover above x. Its given section maps, under the representing isomorphism, to a map V↑→Z. The lifted scheme V↑ is nonempty: a residue-field affine test object at v has nonempty lifted spectrum, and its colimit leg lands in V↑. Applying the map to this point proves Z nonempty.

source.place: Definition 7.3.1 and Lemma 7.3.9: translate a local section into a point of the representing geometric covering

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-normal-geometric-cover-universe-descent] to the etale geometric covering q of X↑ and the point just obtained. All normal-base hypotheses are exactly those of the item. Obtain a finite etale surjective p:Y→X in the original universe and a morphism Y↑→Z over X↑. The cited lemma retains [lem-a1-normal-geometric-cover-components] and adds only the necessary universe transport and small finite-algebra gluing.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71, applied to one connected component of the geometric covering

proof.text: Etaleness implies weak etaleness, so p defines Y as an object of the original pro-etale site directly via ProEt.mk. Bundle the morphism Y↑→Z over X↑ as an arrow in the over category. Evaluate the inverse representing isomorphism on this arrow to obtain a section of F(Y). The finite, etale and surjective properties are those of p.

source.place: Lemma 7.3.9, evaluation of the representing presheaf on the selected finite etale component

I checked its extra conclusions myself: components are open because Z is locally Noetherian, the lifting property restricts to a component because Spec R is connected, and a finite etale component maps onto connected X because its image is open and closed.
